subject: Sampling window, alerting and dashboard entitlement for SLO verification

Subject: Sampling window and alerting entitlements for SLO verification

Hi Logan —

As part of AcmeCorp's procurement review for the Dedicated tier, we have a short questionnaire on how Redwood measures and surfaces SLOs. Can you confirm the following so we can move to legal?

1) Measurement basis — do you use production request telemetry, synthetic probes, or a hybrid? Which is the primary signal for uptime and tail latency SLOs?
2) Sampling/aggregation window — what default rolling window do you use for SLO evaluation (days), and what minute/hour granularity is stored?
3) Cold-start bias — are initial warm-up/cold-starts excluded from the window or tagged separately?
4) Alerting semantics — what constitutes a breach worthy of paging vs an informational alert? Any standard duration thresholds?
5) Customer access — can we get read-only access to dashboards (Grafana) and/or raw query templates (PromQL)? If so, what's the scope and how long are invites valid?
6) Evidence packet — what artifacts do you provide for procurement (dashboard screenshots, retained metrics, export CSVs, SOC2 evidence)?

I've attached our Acme question list (Acme_SLO_Questions.docx) — please reply with short answers and any sample queries or links. Legal prefers concrete examples rather than high-level statements.

Thanks,
Samantha Blake
Senior Cloud Engineer, AcmeCorp
Samantha.Blake@acmecorp.com

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Sampling window and alerting entitlements for SLO verification

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details + artifacts attached for legal: redwood_slo_measurement.pdf. Looping Karthik (runtime) and Marissa (solutions) for anything I miss.

1) Measurement basis: hybrid, with production telemetry as the authoritative source for SLA reporting and synthetic probes as a secondary early-warning signal. Production p95/p99 are used for latency SLOs; availability is derived from successful inference response codes and streaming session health.

2) Sampling/aggregation window: default rolling evaluation window is 28 days (configurable per-account). We store 1-minute aggregates for up to 90 days and 5-minute aggregates for up to 12 months; raw event-level telemetry retained per your contract (can be shortened for privacy).

3) Cold-start bias: we tag requests with cold-start=true for the first inference after model load or scale event; by default cold-starts are excluded from the production SLO calculation but included in raw telemetry for troubleshooting. We can provide a warmed-only percentile variant if you want to exclude warm-up bias entirely.

4) Alerting semantics: informational alerts fire on single-window anomalies (1–2 minute spikes). Pager alerts are triggered when a sustained breach is observed (default: >3x threshold for 5 consecutive minutes or >2% error rate increase sustained for 10 minutes). We publish the alert rules (sample PromQL) and will provide suggested thresholds based on your traffic profile.

5) Customer access: we can grant read-only Grafana views scoped to your routes and models. Invites are tokenized and time-limited; standard is 90 days with renewal, or we can issue a 30-day short-lived token during procurement. We also provide a Prometheus read-only endpoint for agreed queries behind a service account. Instructions attached: grafana-invite-instructions.txt.

6) Evidence packet: attached PDF includes measurement methodology, sample queries, and a screenshot pack. For procurement we typically include 28-day rolling graphs, sample CSV exports, and our SOC2 report link (redacted for non-disclosure).

Action: Marissa — can you prepare a temporary Grafana invite scoped to the Acme routes and add the sample alert rules into the shared Drive link? Karthik — see cold-start note below; confirm the default tag behavior.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com

[Attachment: redwood_slo_measurement.pdf]

Subject: Re: Sampling window and alerting entitlements for SLO verification

Adding a few technical clarifications from the runtime side —

- Cold-start / warm-up: our runtime emits a first-request flag when a model shard loads or when a new pod scales up. Those events are infrequent for steady production but can bias tail percentiles during deploys and large autoscale events. For contractual SLOs we exclude first-request samples from the p95/p99 calculation by default; we can change that if you prefer an inclusive metric.

- Synthetic checks: designed to detect regressions and endpoint liveness; these are kept separate from the SLA signal because synthetics don't reflect heterogeneous customer traffic. We will, however, surface synthetic-derived alerts earlier.

- Aggregation nuance: p95 is computed after removing outliers from deployment windows (we use a 2-step outlier filter documented in the attached PDF). The stored aggregates include tags for model_version, region, and route which you can filter in the Grafana view.

If Acme wants to exclude the first N minutes after a deploy (we can automatically detect deploy windows), we can add a temporary carve-out and annotate the SLO timeline for the procurement evidence.

-Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
